HEADLINE: June home sales disappoint as prices reach an all-time high

blog.headline: June Home Sales Drop as Prices Hit Record Highs: How Builders Are Rethinking Value
blog.angle: June's sales slump amid record prices exposes the tension between affordability and profitability; builders like Lennar respond by redesigning offers and incentives, proving that adapting value propositions is key to sustaining demand when rates bite.

linkedin.headline: Home sales are falling, but builders aren’t slashing prices—they’re rewriting the rules of the deal.
linkedin.angle: When mortgage rates push prices beyond reach, builders face stalled sales; those who engineer affordability instead of chasing volume maintain market relevance.

facebook.headline: June saw home sales dip even as prices hit all-time highs. Lennar isn’t cutting prices—so how are they keeping buyers interested?
facebook.angle: With affordability stretched thin and sales slowing, Lennar’s approach to reshaping deals raises the question: can creative incentives sustain demand when buyers balk?

instagram.headline: High Prices, Falling Sales: Builders Adapt
instagram.angle: Record home prices and slow sales aren’t forcing price cuts—they’re forcing smarter deals and new value plays.

threads.thread_hook: June home sales fell even as prices soared to record highs. Builders aren’t panicking—they’re pivoting.
threads.angle: This thread breaks down how rising rates and record prices create a sales squeeze, and why companies like Lennar are shifting from volume chasing to value engineering to stay afloat.

stories.story_question: Prices hit record highs, but sales are dropping—how do builders keep buyers interested?
stories.angle: Exploring the tension between high prices and affordability, and how adapting offers can sustain demand despite tough market conditions.

images.hook_text: Home sales down, prices at record highs.
